_comment: Antigravity (`agy`) static tool policy — the sandbox-owned half of /root/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json. SEEDED AND MERGED by scripts/profile.sh on every `up`: only the two keys in this file are written, every other key agy stores there (colorScheme, model, trustedWorkspaces, enableTelemetry) is preserved. Run `scripts/profile.sh <profile> reset-antigravity` to re-merge by hand. See sandbox_templates/antigravity/README.md and docs/adr/0006-antigravity-is-two-layer-like-claude.md.
_comment_parity: Mirrors permissions.allow/ask/deny in ../claude/claude-settings.json, converted from Claude's `Bash(x:*)` matcher to agy's `command(x)` grant. BOTH matchers are PREFIX matchers over the command line, so the conversion is one-to-one and the two agents deny the same set. scripts/antigravity-parity.test.sh fails if they ever diverge — that suite is the anti-drift control, so add a command to BOTH files or to neither.
_comment_deny_is_the_tamper_resistant_la: The hard denials live HERE rather than in the PreToolUse hook because a workspace .agents/hooks.json can disable the hook by name (measured — work/0010 Phase 0, test G), and nothing in a workspace can reach settings.json. The hook is defence-in-depth on top of this list, not a substitute for it.
_comment_ask_cache: agy caches an `ask` approval as an Always-Allow grant, so an entry here prompts ONCE, unlike Claude's permissions.ask which re-prompts. The hook re-asserts this set as `force_ask`, which ignores that cache; the static entries below are the backstop for when the hook is not running.
_comment_toolPermission: request-review is already agy's default. Pinning it means a future change to that default, or an accidental `always-proceed`, does not silently widen the profile. Other values: strict, always-proceed, proceed-in-sandbox.

permissions._comment_allow: Read-only inspection, the safe git verbs, project-local build/test runners, and the myclickup read subcommands. Prefix matching: command(ls) covers `ls -la /x`.
permissions._comment_ask: Mutating myclickup subcommands — a write to a real ClickUp workspace is the user's call, not the agent's.
permissions._comment_deny: Network tools, remote VCS, every package installer and fetch-and-run form, shell escapes and interpreter one-liners, and the destructive primitives. Reads of secret FILES are not expressible as a command() grant and are enforced by the hook instead (rule cred-read), which sees view_file, grep_search and run_command alike.
